Set Up

targeted = read_excel('../../doc/targeted/targeted_hormones.xlsx',sheet="DATA",range=NULL)

#convert sex column to factor
targeted$Sex <- as.factor(targeted$Sex)
targeted$`TT (ng/mL)`<- as.numeric(targeted$`TT (ng/mL)`)
targeted$`P4 (ng/mL)`<- as.numeric(targeted$`P4 (ng/mL)`)
targeted$`17B-E2 (ng/mL)`<- as.numeric(targeted$`17B-E2 (ng/mL)`)

#Load Functions
detect_outliers <- function(data, variable) {
  outlier_limit <- quantile(data[[variable]], 0.75, na.rm = TRUE) + 1.5 * IQR(data[[variable]], na.rm = TRUE)
  outliers <- data %>% filter(.data[[variable]] > outlier_limit)
  data %>% filter(.data[[variable]] <= outlier_limit)
  print(outliers)
}

Testosterone Analysis

# Check the p-values
# If  > 0.05, we assume normality and can use a parametric test (t-test)
# Otherwise, use a non-parametric test (Wilcoxon rank-sum test)

if (all_shapiro_tt$p.value > 0.05) {
  # Perform t-test
  tt_t_test <- t.test(`TT (ng/mL)` ~ Sex, data = targeted)
  test_type <- "t-test"
  test_statistic <- tt_t_test$statistic
  p_value <- tt_t_test$p.value
  print(tt_t_test)
} else {
  # Perform Wilcoxon rank-sum test
  tt_wilcox_test <- wilcox.test(`TT (ng/mL)` ~ Sex, data = targeted)
  test_type <- "Wilcoxon rank-sum test"
  test_statistic <- tt_wilcox_test$statistic
  p_value <- tt_wilcox_test$p.value
  print(tt_wilcox_test)
}
## Warning in wilcox.test.default(x = DATA[[1L]], y = DATA[[2L]], ...): cannot
## compute exact p-value with ties
## 
##  Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction
## 
## data:  TT (ng/mL) by Sex
## W = 96, p-value = 0.0002134
## alternative hypothesis: true location shift is not equal to 0
# Visualize results with boxplot
ggboxplot(targeted, x = "Sex", y = "`TT (ng/mL)`",
          color = "Sex", 
          ylab = "TT (ng/mL)", xlab = "Sex",
          add = "jitter") +
  stat_compare_means(method = ifelse(all_shapiro_tt$p.value > 0.05, "t.test", "wilcox.test"),label = "p.format") +
  labs(title = paste(test_type, ": statistic =", round(test_statistic, 2)))

ggsave("tt_statistics_sex.svg", path = svg_path)
## Saving 7 x 5 in image

# Visualize results with boxplot
ggboxplot(targeted, x = "Sex", y = "`P4 (ng/mL)`",
          color = "Sex", 
          ylab = "P4 (ng/mL)", xlab = "Sex",
          add = "jitter") +
  stat_compare_means(method = ifelse(all_shapiro_p4$p.value > 0.05, "t.test", "wilcox.test"),label = "p.format") +
  labs(title = paste(test_type, ": statistic =", round(test_statistic, 2)))

ggsave("p4_statistics_sex.svg", path = svg_path)
## Saving 7 x 5 in image
# Check the p-values
# If  > 0.05, we assume normality and can use a parametric test (t-test)
# Otherwise, use a non-parametric test (Wilcoxon rank-sum test)

if (clean_all_shapiro_p4$p.value > 0.05) {
  # Perform t-test
  clean_p4_t_test <- t.test(`P4 (ng/mL)` ~ Sex, data = clean_targeted)
  test_type <- "t-test"
  test_statistic <- clean_p4_t_test$statistic
  p_value <- clean_p4_t_test$p.value
  print(clean_p4_t_test)
} else {
  # Perform Wilcoxon rank-sum test
  clean_p4_wilcox_test <- wilcox.test(`P4 (ng/mL)` ~ Sex, data = clean_targeted)
  test_type <- "Wilcoxon rank-sum test"
  test_statistic <- clean_p4_wilcox_test$statistic
  p_value <- clean_p4_wilcox_test$p.value
  print(clean_p4_wilcox_test)
}
## 
##  Wilcoxon rank sum exact test
## 
## data:  P4 (ng/mL) by Sex
## W = 302, p-value = 0.3934
## alternative hypothesis: true location shift is not equal to 0
# Visualize results with boxplot
ggboxplot(clean_targeted, x = "Sex", y = "`P4 (ng/mL)`",
          color = "Sex", 
          ylab = "P4 (ng/mL)", xlab = "Sex",
          add = "jitter") +
  stat_compare_means(method = ifelse(clean_all_shapiro_p4$p.value > 0.05, "t.test", "wilcox.test"),label = "p.format") +
  labs(title = paste(test_type, ": statistic =", round(test_statistic, 2)))

ggsave("clean_p4_statistics_sex.svg", path = svg_path)
